conflicts.description: The same customer identity is named custid in bank1 and customer_id in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized the unified identity name as customer_id.

conflicts.description: The account identity is represented as an account number in bank1 and an account identifier in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized the entity key as account_id while retaining provenance from both source keys.

conflicts.description: Equivalent account attributes use abbreviated versus descriptive names.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted descriptive snake_case names account_type and account_balance_amount.

conflicts.description: Branch attributes use generic names in bank1 and entity-qualified names in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted branch_name and branch_address to eliminate ambiguous homonyms.

conflicts.description: Equivalent customer telephone attributes use phone and mobileno.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized the attribute as phone_number.

conflicts.description: The customer-loan relationship is named availed_by in bank1 and borrower in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Named the normalized relationship resource loan_borrower.

conflicts.description: The source table name includes an informational suffix rather than naming the entity directly.
conflicts.resolution: Renamed the target entity resource to banker.

conflicts.description: The source table embeds ownership context in the credit-card entity name.
conflicts.resolution: Named the target entity credit_card and represented ownership with a customer_id foreign key.

conflicts.description: Account balance is number in bank1 but integer in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Used number to preserve fractional monetary values and safely accommodate both representations.

conflicts.description: Loan principal is number in bank1 but integer in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Used number for the unified issued_amount.

conflicts.description: Monetary quantities are encoded as integers, which may prevent representation of fractional currency amounts.
conflicts.resolution: Used the generic number type for monetary measures in the target.

conflicts.description: bank1 supplies one undifferentiated loan amount, while bank2 distinguishes issued principal from the remaining balance.
conflicts.resolution: Interpreted bank1 amount as original principal and unified it with issued_amount; retained remaining_amount as a separate attribute to avoid conflating principal and outstanding balance.

conflicts.description: The schemas contain monetary values without currency codes or declared minor-unit scales.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved values as number fields with amount-qualified names and documented that currency is unspecified; no unsupported currency conversion was inferred.

conflicts.description: Addresses are supplied as opaque strings, so their internal component semantics cannot be reliably aligned or split.
conflicts.resolution: Retained each address as an atomic source-supplied string rather than inventing unverified street, locality, or postal-code components.

conflicts.description: Customer-account ownership is modeled as a separate association table in bank1 but embedded as an account foreign key on customer in bank2.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized ownership into the customer_account relationship resource.

conflicts.description: Account-branch maintenance is represented both as a relationship table and as embedded foreign keys.
conflicts.resolution: Centralized the relationship in account_branch and removed branch_id from the account entity.

conflicts.description: Loan-branch association is represented both as an offer table and as embedded branch foreign keys.
conflicts.resolution: Centralized the relationship in loan_branch and removed branch_id from the loan entity.

conflicts.description: One schema uses a pure bridge while the other uses a relationship entity with its own identifier.
conflicts.resolution: Used a normalized loan_borrower bridge and retained bank2's relationship identifier as a source-specific non-key attribute.

conflicts.description: bank1 explicitly models banks and their branches, whereas bank2 begins at the branch level and has no bank entity or bank reference.
conflicts.resolution: Retained bank as an optional higher-level entity and made branch.bank_code nullable for sources without bank-level data.

conflicts.description: bank1 permits many-to-many customer-account holdings, while bank2 records one account reference per customer row.
conflicts.resolution: Used a many-to-many customer_account bridge, which preserves bank1 joint holdings and represents bank2's narrower relationship without loss.

conflicts.description: The maintain bridge can express multiple branches per account, while embedded branch_id columns imply one branch per account.
conflicts.resolution: Used account_branch with a composite key to support the more general many-to-many cardinality.

conflicts.description: The offer bridge can associate a loan with multiple branches, while direct branch_id columns imply one branch per loan.
conflicts.resolution: Used loan_branch with a composite key to preserve the more general relationship.

conflicts.description: Both sources permit customer-loan associations, but bank2 can technically contain multiple borrower rows for the same customer and loan because borrower_id is its key.
conflicts.resolution: Defined one canonical customer-loan association per composite pair and retained the source borrower identifier for lineage.

conflicts.description: Several bank1 primary-key declarations use capitalization that does not match the actual lowercase field names.
conflicts.resolution: Defined valid lowercase composite keys using the actual normalized relationship fields.

conflicts.description: bank1 contains duplicate foreign-key declarations, including case-variant references to fields that do not exist with the declared capitalization.
conflicts.resolution: Removed duplicate and invalid case-variant declarations and retained one valid foreign key per relationship.

conflicts.description: bank2 repeats each listed foreign-key declaration.
conflicts.resolution: Deduplicated foreign keys in the unified schema.

conflicts.description: bank1 keys the borrower relationship by customer and loan, while bank2 uses a surrogate borrower_id.
conflicts.resolution: Used the semantically meaningful composite customer_id and loan_id as the global key and retained borrower_id separately for source traceability.

conflicts.description: Equivalent account entities use differently named primary keys.
conflicts.resolution: Unified them under account_id with both source primary keys recorded in provenance.

conflicts.description: Equivalent customer entities use differently named primary keys.
conflicts.resolution: Unified them under customer_id with both source primary keys recorded in provenance.
